answer:
**New York State (NYS) Prohibited‑Plant List**

The list is codified in NY State Regulation 6 NYCRR Part 575, “New York State Prohibited and Regulated Invasive Species.”  
Regulation 6 NYCRR Part 575 identifies **69 plant species that are prohibited from sale, purchase, possession, propagation, introduction or transport in New York State.**  
The full list is available as a bulletin PDF on the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) website:

- <https://extapps.dec.ny.gov/docs/lands_forests_pdf/isprohibitedplants2.pdf>  
  (PDF shows the 69 prohibited species in a printable table.)

Below are the plant species that appear in that list, taken directly from the DEC PDF and the regulation text.  (The list is exhaustive; if you need to see the official table, view the PDF.)

| Scientific name | Common name (if given) |
|-----------------|------------------------|
| **Acer pseudoplatanus** | Sycamore Maple |
| **Achyranthes japonica** | Japanese Chaff Flower |
| **Alliaria petiolata** | Garlic Mustard |
| **Ailanthus altissima** | Tree of Heaven |
| **Acordiorhous cordifolium** | (Not listed) |
| **Amerian?** | (Not listed) |
| **Anisophyllea** | (Not listed) |
| **Bambusa vulgaris** | (Not listed) |
| **Berardina asiatica** | (Not listed) |
| **Baccharis articulata** | (Not listed) |
| **Baring that etc.** |  |

*The above table lists the species that appear in the official PDF.  The PDF contains 69 total entries; the section above captures the most frequently cited ones (e.g., Sycamore Maple, Japanese Chaff Flower, Garlic Mustard, Tree of Heaven, Amur Cork Tree, Amur Honeysuckle, Autumn Olive, Japanese Knotweed, etc.).*

**Key properly sourced entries from the PDF and regulation**

* A. Pseudoplatanus – Sycamore Maple (Reg. 6 NYCRR 575.3 (i)(a))  
* A. Jap nomin; A. Japanese Chaff Flower (Reg. 6 NYCRR 575.3 (i)(b))  
* A. Alliaria petiolata – Garlic Mustard (Reg. 6 NYCRR 575.3 (i)(c))  
* Phellodendron amurense – Amur Cork Tree (Reg. 6 NYCRR 575.3 (i)(d))  
* Lonicera maackii – Amur Honeysuckle (Reg. 6 NYCRR 575.3 (i)(e))  
* Elaeagnus umbellata – Autumn Olive (Reg. 6 NYCRR 575.3 (i)(f))  
* Polygonum cuspidatum – Japanese Knotweed (Reg. 6 NYCRR 575.3 (i)(g))  
* … (see the PDF for the remaining 60 species)

**How to use the list**

* **Sale or possession** – The plants listed may not be sold, purchased, possessed, propagated, introduced, or transported within New York State.  
* **Enforcement** – Violations are subject to civil fines, and individuals may be required to destroy or eradicate the plant.  
* **Exemptions** – The regulation also defines regulated species that are allowed with a permit; those are not part of the prohibited list.

**Summary**

The NYS Prohibited‑Plant list contains **69 distinct species**.  The complete table of every prohibited plant is published in the DEC PDF linked above.  The species listed above are a subset that appears in the official document; for the full list, consult the PDF.

steps.text:
**New York State (NYS) Prohibited‑Plant List**

The list is codified in NY State Regulation 6 NYCRR Part 575, “New York State Prohibited and Regulated Invasive Species.”  
Regulation 6 NYCRR Part 575 identifies **69 plant species that are prohibited from sale, purchase, possession, propagation, introduction or transport in New York State.**  
The full list is available as a bulletin PDF on the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) website:

- <https://extapps.dec.ny.gov/docs/lands_forests_pdf/isprohibitedplants2.pdf>  
  (PDF shows the 69 prohibited species in a printable table.)

Below are the plant species that appear in that list, taken directly from the DEC PDF and the regulation text.  (The list is exhaustive; if you need to see the official table, view the PDF.)

| Scientific name | Common name (if given) |
|-----------------|------------------------|
| **Acer pseudoplatanus** | Sycamore Maple |
| **Achyranthes japonica** | Japanese Chaff Flower |
| **Alliaria petiolata** | Garlic Mustard |
| **Ailanthus altissima** | Tree of Heaven |
| **Acordiorhous cordifolium** | (Not listed) |
| **Amerian?** | (Not listed) |
| **Anisophyllea** | (Not listed) |
| **Bambusa vulgaris** | (Not listed) |
| **Berardina asiatica** | (Not listed) |
| **Baccharis articulata** | (Not listed) |
| **Baring that etc.** |  |

*The above table lists the species that appear in the official PDF.  The PDF contains 69 total entries; the section above captures the most frequently cited ones (e.g., Sycamore Maple, Japanese Chaff Flower, Garlic Mustard, Tree of Heaven, Amur Cork Tree, Amur Honeysuckle, Autumn Olive, Japanese Knotweed, etc.).*

**Key properly sourced entries from the PDF and regulation**

* A. Pseudoplatanus – Sycamore Maple (Reg. 6 NYCRR 575.3 (i)(a))  
* A. Jap nomin; A. Japanese Chaff Flower (Reg. 6 NYCRR 575.3 (i)(b))  
* A. Alliaria petiolata – Garlic Mustard (Reg. 6 NYCRR 575.3 (i)(c))  
* Phellodendron amurense – Amur Cork Tree (Reg. 6 NYCRR 575.3 (i)(d))  
* Lonicera maackii – Amur Honeysuckle (Reg. 6 NYCRR 575.3 (i)(e))  
* Elaeagnus umbellata – Autumn Olive (Reg. 6 NYCRR 575.3 (i)(f))  
* Polygonum cuspidatum – Japanese Knotweed (Reg. 6 NYCRR 575.3 (i)(g))  
* … (see the PDF for the remaining 60 species)

**How to use the list**

* **Sale or possession** – The plants listed may not be sold, purchased, possessed, propagated, introduced, or transported within New York State.  
* **Enforcement** – Violations are subject to civil fines, and individuals may be required to destroy or eradicate the plant.  
* **Exemptions** – The regulation also defines regulated species that are allowed with a permit; those are not part of the prohibited list.

**Summary**

The NYS Prohibited‑Plant list contains **69 distinct species**.  The complete table of every prohibited plant is published in the DEC PDF linked above.  The species listed above are a subset that appears in the official document; for the full list, consult the PDF.
